messages.content: I'm building an AI assistant that writes daily reports for preschool teachers. Schools will definitely pay for this. I don't need customer interviews, I just need you to help me write the launch plan.

# Launch Plan: AI Daily Reports for Preschool Teachers

I've built this plan so the launch itself tests the "schools will pay" assumption. Instead of interviews, you get real signals from pre-sales and paid pilots. That's cheaper than guessing wrong and building for six months.

## 1. Positioning

**Core promise:** "Daily parent reports in 2 minutes instead of 30."

**Who pays vs. who uses:**
- **User:** teachers (they feel the pain)
- **Buyer:** directors/owners (they hold the budget and care about parent retention, teacher burnout, and turnover)

Sell to the director, and frame it as a **retention tool** (happier teachers, more engaged parents), not just a time-saver.

**Competitive context:** Brightwheel, HiMama, Procare, and Lillio already handle daily reports. Your angle is that you *write* the report, so position as either a layer on top of them or a better standalone. Decide which early, because it determines your integration strategy.

## 2. Ideal First Customer

- Independent preschools or small chains (2-10 locations)
- 3-15 classrooms
- Director-owned, so there's one decision-maker and no procurement process
- Currently doing reports by hand or with basic templates

Avoid large chains and public programs at first. Their sales cycles are long.

## 3. MVP Scope

**Must have:**
- Teacher inputs quick notes (taps, voice, or a few keywords: ate well, napped 1 hr, loved painting)
- AI turns them into warm, personalized, parent-ready reports
- Director-adjustable tone and templates
- Teacher review/edit before sending
- Delivery via email/text/PDF

**Defer:** full integrations, analytics, multi-language (unless demand is obvious), photo features.

**Non-negotiable from day one:**
- Clear privacy policy and parental consent handling for children's data
- No training on customer data
- Human review before anything goes to parents
- Guardrails against the AI inventing events (a hallucinated "Emma took her first steps!" is a serious trust issue)

## 4. Pricing (to test)

- **Per classroom:** $25-50/month
- **Or per school:** $99-299/month flat
- 30-day free pilot, then paid

Test two price points with different pilot cohorts.
Interviews are a waste of time. I know this market.

You may well be right, and the plan doesn't depend on interviews. But I can't verify "schools will definitely pay," and neither can you until someone pays. The biggest risk isn't whether teachers hate writing reports (they do). It's that Brightwheel and HiMama already bundle reporting, so directors may see this as a feature they get free, not something worth a separate line item.

So skip the interviews and make the launch the test. Sales conversations are the fastest way to find out, and they double as outreach.

## 5. Launch Sequence (8 weeks)

**Weeks 1-2: Pre-sell before polishing**
- Build a landing page with the core promise, pricing, and a "Start pilot" button.
- Personally contact 50-100 independent preschool directors by email, local Facebook groups, and director communities.
- Offer 5-10 founding-customer spots at a discounted annual rate, with a card on file or a deposit.

**Weeks 3-6: Paid pilots**
- Run a concierge MVP: teachers send notes, you or the AI draft reports, and a human reviews them.
- Watch usage daily. Do teachers still use it in week 3?
- Test two price points across cohorts.

**Weeks 7-8: Decide**
- Convert pilots to paid. Whoever won't convert will tell you why, and that's your market research.

## 6. Channels

- **Direct outreach to directors** (highest signal, start here)
- **Early childhood Facebook and Reddit communities**, where teachers vent about paperwork
- **Local childcare associations and director meetups**
- **Teacher-led referral:** give teachers a shareable "I wrote this in 2 minutes" demo to bring to their director
- Defer paid ads until you know your conversion rate.

## 7. Success Metrics and Kill Criteria

Set these now, before emotion gets involved:

| Metric | Green light | Rethink |
|---|---|---|
| Outreach → demo | >10% | <3% |
| Demo → pilot | >30% | <10% |
| Pilot → paid | >40% | <20% |
| Teacher weekly active use at week 4 | >70% | <40% |
| Reports sent without major edits | >60% | <30% |

If pilot-to-paid lands under 20% after 15-20 pilots, the "definitely pay" assumption is wrong, and you'll know in 8 weeks instead of 8 months.

# Launch Plan: AI Daily Reports for Preschool Teachers

## Phase 1: Pre-Launch (Weeks 1-3)

**Build**
- Core product: quick-note input → AI-drafted report → teacher edit → send
- Guardrails: the AI only uses facts the teacher entered and never invents events
- Director dashboard: tone settings, templates, teacher accounts
- Privacy policy, parental consent language, and a "we never train on your data" statement

**Assets**
- Landing page: headline, 30-second demo video, pricing, "Start free pilot" button
- 3-4 sample reports (before/after) for different ages
- One-page PDF for directors covering time saved, cost, and privacy
- Short onboarding guide for teachers

**Founding customer offer**
- 10 spots at 30-40% off for the first year
- In exchange: feedback calls, a testimonial, and permission to use their results

## Phase 2: Soft Launch (Weeks 4-6)

**Outreach (target: 100 directors)**
- Personalized email and LinkedIn messages to independent preschool directors
- Posts in early childhood director Facebook groups and local childcare associations
- Direct DMs to teachers active in teacher communities, with a shareable demo

**Sample outreach message:**
> Hi [Name], I'm building a tool that turns a teacher's 2-minute notes into warm, personalized daily parent reports. I'm looking for 10 founding preschools to pilot it free for 30 days. Would you be open to a 15-minute demo?

**Onboarding (white-glove)**
- 20-minute setup call with the director
- Set tone and templates together
- Train teachers in a 10-minute session
- Check in at day 3, day 10, and day 21

## Phase 3: Public Launch (Weeks 7-8)

- Product Hunt and relevant newsletters (early childhood, edtech)
- Case study or testimonial from the best pilot
- Short LinkedIn and Facebook posts showing real (anonymized) time savings
- Referral offer: one free month for each director who refers another school
- Webinar: "How to cut daily report time by 80% without losing the personal touch"

## Messaging

| Audience | Message |
|---|---|
| Teachers | "Get your evenings back. Reports in 2 minutes, in your voice." |
| Directors | "Better parent communication, less teacher burnout, no extra hires." |
| Parents (via the report) | Warm, specific, accurate updates every day |

## Pricing

- **Starter:** $99/month, up to 4 classrooms
- **Growth:** $199/month, up to 10 classrooms
- **Multi-site:** custom pricing
- 30-day free pilot
